package org.firstinspires.ftc.teamcode.opmodes;

import com.pedropathing.api.Paths;
import com.pedropathing.api.PoseFactory;
import com.pedropathing.math.Pose;
import com.pedropathing.paths.Path;

import org.firstinspires.ftc.teamcode.config.MatchState;
import org.firstinspires.ftc.teamcode.config.Tuned;

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;

// Generated by refract-suite ftc-construct. PLACEHOLDER in the shape of a Pedro visualizer "Class" export
// (BIOBUZZ field, drawn on the BLUE side). To use a real path: paste the export's pose fields and Path
// methods here, keep the poseFactory line as MatchState.poseFactory() (red = 180-degree rotation), never
// tick the visualizer's mirror option, wrap a pose in redTrim(...) if red needs a field correction, and
// list the legs with their action in legs().
public class AutoPaths {
    private final PoseFactory poseFactory = MatchState.poseFactory();

    private final Pose start = redTrim(poseFactory.of(Tuned.blueStartX, Tuned.blueStartY, Tuned.blueStartHeading), 0, 0, 0);
    private final Pose park = redTrim(poseFactory.of(Tuned.blueParkX, Tuned.blueParkY, Tuned.blueParkHeading), 0, 0, 0);

    public static boolean ready() {
        return Tuned.isSet(Tuned.blueStartX, Tuned.blueStartY, Tuned.blueStartHeading,
                Tuned.blueParkX, Tuned.blueParkY, Tuned.blueParkHeading);
    }

    // Red-only field correction (in, deg) added after the 180-degree rotation, for differences between the
    // two halves of a real field found in practice. DECODE 19859 needed 1-3 in on its close auto because
    // its red side was a mirror (robot turns flipped); a rotation keeps the robot's motion identical, so
    // expect these to stay near 0. Blue ignores them.
    private static Pose redTrim(Pose pose, double dx, double dy, double dHeadingDeg) {
        if (MatchState.alliance != MatchState.Alliance.RED) return pose;
        return new Pose(pose.x() + dx, pose.y() + dy, pose.heading() + Math.toRadians(dHeadingDeg));
    }

    public Pose start() {
        return start;
    }

    public Path toPark() {
        return Paths.line(start, park).linear(start, park);
    }

    public List<AutoRunner.Leg> legs() {
        return Arrays.asList(new AutoRunner.Leg(toPark(), AutoRunner.Action.PARK));
    }
}
